result.topic_en: Euler gives the recursion for the coefficients expressing the sums of reciprocal powers of odd numbers (alternating for odd powers) in terms of powers of q, tabulates them, relates them to ζ(2n)-type fractions 1/6, 1/90, 1/945, 1/9450, and begins deriving a logarithmic series from Wallis-type infinite products.
result.transcription:
512 \quad L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. \quad Analysis.

$1-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{7}+\frac{1}{9}-\frac{1}{11}+$ etc. $=Aq.$
$1+\frac{1}{3^2}+\frac{1}{5^2}+\frac{1}{7^2}+\frac{1}{9^2}+\frac{1}{11^2}+$ etc. $=2Bqq.$
$1-\frac{1}{3^3}+\frac{1}{5^3}-\frac{1}{7^3}+\frac{1}{9^3}-\frac{1}{11^3}+$ etc. $=4Cq^3$
$1+\frac{1}{3^4}+\frac{1}{5^4}+\frac{1}{7^4}+\frac{1}{9^4}+\frac{1}{11^4}+$ etc. $=8Dq^4$
etc.

coefficientes ita a se invicem pendent, ut sit
$A=1,\quad B=1,\quad C=\frac{2AB}{4},\quad D=\frac{2AC+BB}{6},\quad E=\frac{2AD+2BC}{8},\quad F=\frac{2AE+2BD+CC}{10},$ etc.
unde colliguntur isti valores
$A=1,\quad B=1,\quad C=\frac{1}{2},\quad D=\frac{1}{3},\quad E=\frac{5}{24},\quad F=\frac{2}{15},\quad G=\frac{61}{720},\quad H=\frac{17}{315}$ etc.,
ubi insuper litterae seorsim per 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 etc. multiplicari debent. Hinc istos numeros ulterius continuavi, quos ergo cum potestatibus ipsius $q$ sequenti modo repraesento. Prior columna valet pro potestatibus imparibus, posterior vero pro paribus:

$Aq\ =1.q$ \qquad $Bq^2\ =1.2q^2$
$Cq^3=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4q^3$ \qquad $Dq^4=\frac{1}{3}\cdot 8q^4$
$Eq^5=\frac{5}{8.3}\cdot 16q^5$ \qquad $Fq^6=\frac{2}{3.5}\cdot 32q^6$
$Gq^7=\frac{61}{16.9.5}\cdot 64q^7$ \qquad $Hq^8=\frac{17}{9.5.7}\cdot 128q^8$
$Jq^9=\frac{277}{128.9.7}\cdot 256q^9$ \qquad $Kq^{10}=\frac{2.31}{81.5.7}\cdot 512q^{10}$
$Lq^{11}=\frac{19.2659}{256\ 81.25.7}\cdot 1024q^{11}$ \qquad $Mq^{12}=\frac{2.691}{81.25.7.11}\cdot 2048q^{12}$
etc. \qquad etc.

Quodsi litterae posterioris columnae ordine dividantur per hos numeros 2.3, 2.15, 2.63, etc. prodeunt meae fractiones $\frac{1}{6},\ \frac{1}{90},\ \frac{1}{945},\ \frac{1}{9450}$, etc.
Supra habuimus haec duo producta
$\frac{\pi}{4}\cdot\frac{4}{3}\cdot\frac{4}{5}\cdot\frac{8}{7}\cdot\frac{12}{11}\cdot\frac{12}{13}\cdot$ etc. $=1$ et $\frac{\pi}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{3}\cdot\frac{6}{5}\cdot\frac{6}{7}\cdot\frac{10}{11}\cdot\frac{14}{13}\cdot$ etc. $=1$;
horum prius per posterius divisum dat: $1\cdot\frac{4}{6}\cdot\frac{8}{6}\cdot\frac{12}{10}\cdot\frac{12}{14}\cdot\frac{16}{18}\cdot\frac{20}{22}\cdot$ etc. $=1$. Hae fractiones invertantur et sumantur logarithmi, eritque
$l\frac{6}{4}+l\frac{6}{8}+l\frac{10}{12}+l\frac{14}{12}+$ etc. $=0.$
Cum igitur sit $l\frac{6}{4}=l\frac{1+\frac{1}{5}}{1-\frac{1}{5}}$, $l\frac{6}{8}=l\frac{1-\frac{1}{7}}{1+\frac{1}{7}}$, etc. evolutis logarithmis semissis dabit hanc aequationem:

items.quote: Quodsi litterae posterioris columnae ordine dividantur per hos numeros 2.3, 2.15, 2.63, etc. prodeunt meae fractiones $\frac{1}{6},\ \frac{1}{90},\ \frac{1}{945},\ \frac{1}{9450}$, etc.
items.english: If the letters of the latter column are divided in order by these numbers 2.3, 2.15, 2.63, etc., my fractions 1/6, 1/90, 1/945, 1/9450, etc. result.
